report:
There is medial meniscal extrusion at the level of the body, deemed secondary to an undisplaced degenerative type tear through the corresponding posterior horn and root.  
Mildly degenerate but otherwise intact lateral meniscus, normal cruciate and collateral ligaments, popliteus, patellar tendon and distal iliotibial band. Chronic, quiescent looking calcific distal insertional quadriceps tendinopathy is present anteriorly. 
 No fracture or marrow infiltration, minimal intra-articular fluid, probably within normal physiological limits.  Mild age-related thinning of tricompartmental articular cartilage, probably most apparent at the medial weightbearing compartment. Tiny focus of high-grade cartilage loss with associated faint focal reactive marrow changes is noted adjacent to the median ridge of the patella.  Small focus of grade 3 cartilage loss noted at the central portion of the lateral tibial plateau. Grossly unremarkable imaged extra-articular soft tissues.

МР находка: МР данни за контузионен костномозъчен едем в кондилите на фемура и тибията. Отокът в тибията е локализиран предимно срединно под интеркондиларните еминенции. Ставният хрущял на фемура и тибията е запазен. МР данни за руптура на предна кръстна връзка. Последната е едемна, с уголемен напречник. Виждат се едемни изменения и висок сигнален интензитет в проксималното залавно място на латералния колатерален лигамент. Последният е със запазен континуитет и лекостепенно нагънат ход. Дегенеративни промени в заден рог на медиалния менискус. Нормално изобразяване на латералния менискус. Визуализира се перисиновиална киста на нивото на медиалната глава на м. гастрокнемиус. Патела, хрущял на пателата, ретинакулуми – без особености. Наличие на ставен излив. Заключение:  МР данни за руптура на предна кръстна връзка. Контузионен костномозъчен едем във фемура и тибията. Частична увреда на латералния колатерален лигамент. Ставен излив.

MRI LEFT KNEE:

INDICATION:    Lateral left knee pain for 6 weeks not improving on physiotherapy. Occurred during marathon training. X-rays within normal limits.

PRIOR IMAGING: None.
.
TECHNICAL INFORMATION AND PROTOCOL:

Proton density and T2 weighted sagittal, coronal and axial imaging was performed through the knee including a 3D Fat suppressed proton density weighted sequence. No contrast was administered.

FINDINGS:

The 3-D proton density sequence was reformatted and manipulated to aid in the interpretation of this examination.

The extensor mechanism including quadriceps and patellar tendons is intact and appears unremarkable. The patellofemoral ligaments are intact and appear unremarkable. The articular cartilage of the patellofemoral joint is well-maintained. The TT-TG distance is within normal limits at about 1 cm.

The lateral meniscus is intact. The articular cartilage of the lateral joint compartment is well-maintained.

The medial meniscus is intact. The articular cartilage of the medial joint compartment is well-maintained.

The anterior cruciate ligament, posterior cruciate ligament, medial collateral ligament and lateral collateral ligament complex including the IT band, fibular collateral ligament, popliteus tendon and biceps femoris tendon all appear intact and unremarkable. No features of IT band syndrome to explain lateral joint margin pain.

There is no Baker's cyst demonstrated. No significant knee effusion.

Marrow signal is within normal limits.

INTERPRETATION: 

There is no evidence of internal derangement.

No definite cause is identified for the lateral knee pain noted clinically.

> Abnormal signal intensity is noted in low pole patella and distal femur (lateral femoral condyle), which shows low signal intensity on T1WI and high signal intensity on T2WI, in favor of bone contusion.
> Laxity and increased signal intensity of the medial patellar retinaculum, R/O grade 1-2 strain
> The contour of ACL & PCL appear to be within normal, no abnormal signal intensity is noted.
> No evidence of tear is noted in either medial or lateral meniscus.
> Both medial & lateral collateral ligaments appear to be within normal.

Impression: 
1. Lateral subluxation of patella with bone contusion at lateral femoral condyle and low pole of patella; R/O tiny avulsion fracture of medial aspect of low pole patella and associated grade 1-2 strain medial patellar retinaculum.
2. Large amount of joint effusion with synovitis and suprapatellar bursitis and complex plicae.
3. Bone contusion at lateral femoral condyle with R/O impaction fracture at lateral aspect of lateral femoral condyle (se:5, Im:12)
Suggest correlation with clinical manifestation
